'''Ann S. Almgren''' is an American applied mathematician who works as a senior scientist and group leader of the Center for Computational Sciences and Engineering at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. Her primary research interests are in computational algorithms for solving [[Partial differential equation|PDE]]'s for fluid dynamics in a variety of application areas. Her current projects include the development and implementation of new multiphysics algorithms in high-resolution adaptive mesh codes that are designed for the
latest multicore architectures.<ref>{{citation|url=https://ccse.lbl.gov/people/almgren/|title=Staff profile: Ann S. Almgren|publisher=LBL|access-date=2015-10-09}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Almgren is the daughter of mathematician [[Frederick J. Almgren, Jr.]] and his first wife, Beverly Stewart.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Taylor | first = Jean E. | author-link = Jean Taylor
 | doi = 10.1007/BF02922664
 | issue = 5
 | journal = The Journal of Geometric Analysis
 | mr = 1731056
 | pages = 679–680
 | title = Frederick Justin Almgren, 1933–1997
 | volume = 8
 | year = 1998| s2cid = 122052098 }}.</ref> She earned a bachelor's degree in [[physics]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1984 and a master's degree in [[mechanical engineering]] from [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1987. Her doctoral degree in mechanical engineering was completed in 1991 at UC Berkeley under the direction of [[Phillip Colella]] with a dissertation titled ''A Fast Adaptive Vortex Method in Three Dimensions''.<ref name="diss">{{cite thesis |last=Almgren |first=Ann Stewart |date=1991 |title=A Fast Adaptive Vortex Method in Three Dimensions |degree=PhD |publisher=University of California at Berkeley |url=https://crd.lbl.gov/assets/pubs_presos/AMCS/ANAG/AlmgrenThesis.pdf |access-date=November 23, 2024}}</ref> After visiting the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], she joined the applied mathematics group of the [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] in 1992, and moved to the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] in 1996.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://ccse.lbl.gov/people/almgren/cv_almgren_2014.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Ann S. Almgren|publisher=LBL|access-date=2015-10-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304075000/https://ccse.lbl.gov/people/almgren/cv_almgren_2014.pdf|archive-date=2016-03-04|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2015 she became a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] "for contributions to the development of numerical methods for fluid dynamics and applying them to large-scale scientific and engineering problems."<ref>{{citation|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2015|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2015|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|access-date=2015-10-08}}.</ref>  She also serves on the editorial boards of SIREV<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/journals/sirev/board.php|title=SIREV &#124; Editorial Board &#124; SIAM}}</ref> and CAMCoS<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://msp.org/camcos/about/journal/editorial.html|title = CAMCoS Editorial}}</ref>
